solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Praise fruit Australia's imported

indicators.note: imported means brought into something, so Australia's abbreviation is carried inside the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
AUS is the standard abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: A boast that Australian fruit has been brought in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping an act is a way of expressing approval, so the noun works as a synonym for acclaim.

clue.text: A problem? Not describing this clue!

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden or trouble, so cross means a problem

explanation.surface: A self-referential puzzle that pretends to be asking whether something is a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is witty: this clue sits in the down list, so the direction it does not describe is the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues run either horizontally or vertically; this one is vertical, so the word it does not describe is the horizontal direction.

clue.text: Medicine that's painful: sleep on it

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine
ow is the cry made when something hurts

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice: the tablet stings, so take it and sleep it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleep on it' sounds like advice to wait before deciding, but it literally describes the cushion under your head.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing you rest your head on in bed is the soft cushion, so you literally sleep on it.

clue.text: Knowing conflict is in abeyance, all content to leave

indicators.note: is in tells us the word for conflict sits inside what remains of the other word
the content of a word is everything between its ends, so removing it leaves only the outer letters

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Someone shrewd notes that a dispute has been suspended and everyone is happy to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all content to leave' reads as everyone being happy to depart, but it strips abeyance to its outer letters, AE.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing and conscious of something are close synonyms, as in being alert to a situation.

clue.text: Musician's stool is broken

definitions.note: read as 'musician is', the 's being the link to the wordplay

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of stool is are reassembled

explanation.surface: A performer complains that their stool has broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who plays alone, without accompaniment, is a type of musician.

clue.text: Escaped nasty duel at end — knight went missing

indicators.note: a nasty duel is a messy one, so its letters are rearranged
went missing says the knight's letter disappears from the word before it

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: After an ugly duel, a knight vanished and got away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' scrambles DUEL into ELUD; 'went missing' takes N from END, leaving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have evaded or slipped away from pursuers is to have escaped them.

clue.text: Offensive swearing in African port

indicators.note: in places the swearing word inside the name of the port

parts.note: Lome is the capital and port of Togo in West Africa
oaths are swear words or curses

explanation.surface: Bad language heard in a harbour city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent or detestable is offensive, a near synonym.

clue.text: Get rid of the drone somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of the drone arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove an annoying drone by any means.
explanation.walkthrough: A drone is also an idle male bee, so the surface hints at a hive; the answer removes a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a ruler from the throne is to get rid of them from power.

clue.text: Maybe dog's cross, upset, seeing where canvasser may go

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dog is an example of pets, the 'Maybe' marking it as one instance
a rood is a crucifix, a cross

explanation.surface: A grumpy dog that is clearly annoyed greets a political campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an angry dog, but it is the crucifix; 'upset' signals reading upwards in this down entry, and 'Maybe' marks dog as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes from house to house asking for votes, standing at each front step.

clue.text: Referring to Light Infantry, skilled and trustworthy

parts.note: re means about, concerning
LI is the military abbreviation for Light Infantry
able means capable, skilled

explanation.surface: A report on a regiment praising its soldiers as competent and dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependable and trustworthy are synonyms.

clue.text: Permanently mark military spectacle

definitions.meaning: to ink a design into the skin, a verb
a show of marching bands and drill, such as the Edinburgh one

explanation.surface: An army display leaves an indelible impression.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an inked skin design and an evening military display with drums and bands.

clue.text: Receiving lecture at outset, sulk and hide

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the sulk word takes in a letter

parts.note: to be in a pet is to be in a sulk

indicators.note: at outset picks the opening letter of lecture

explanation.surface: A child given a telling-off sulks and goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb meaning conceal, but it is the noun: an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's skin with the fur still on is a hide.

clue.text: Water alongside this wandering isle heron

indicators.note: wandering means roaming about, so the letters of isle heron move into a new order

explanation.surface: A heron roams about an island, near the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of land where it meets the sea is the place that has water beside it.

clue.text: Author usefully displays object of worship

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer helpfully puts on show something people revere.
explanation.definitionFit: The falcon-headed sky god of ancient Egypt was worshipped, so he is an object of worship.

clue.text: History period at Saint Trinian's starts

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A history lesson at St Trinian's, the anarchic girls' school of British films and cartoons.
explanation.walkthrough: St Trinian's is a fictional unruly British girls' school from Ronald Searle's cartoons and films.
explanation.definitionFit: Bygone times and history both mean what has gone before.

clue.text: After a contest, be confronted by sharp change

indicators.note: after says the confronting word comes behind the first two pieces

parts.note: a bout is a fight or contest
to face something is to be confronted by it

explanation.surface: Following a fight, someone meets an abrupt reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or direction is a sharp change, from the drill turn.

clue.text: Heavily defeat Right, suffering setback, vitality lacking at first

indicators.note: a setback turns things backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation of right, as in Rt Hon

indicators.note: lacking at first says the first letter of the vitality word is dropped

parts.note: bounce means liveliness or vitality

explanation.surface: A political right wing suffers a reverse and loses its energy, being thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' turns RT into TR; 'lacking at first' drops B from BOUNCE to leave OUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent soundly, to thrash them, is to defeat heavily.

clue.text: Highly doubtful son at university acted as model!

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
up means in residence at university, as at Oxford or Cambridge
posed means sat for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A student son claims to have modelled, a dubious story.
explanation.definitionFit: Something merely assumed or alleged, rather than proven, is of doubtful truth.

clue.text: On return, arrest four in camp originally nonmilitary

indicators.note: on return says the pieces are read backwards, up the down light

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch or arrest them
IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of each of in and camp

explanation.surface: Detaining four people in a camp who turned out to be ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes I and C from 'in camp'; 'On return' reverses NAIL IV IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A person not in the armed forces is a nonmilitary one.

clue.text: Regular fun or I'm wretched!

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters of fun or I'm are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that ordinary fun leaves them miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvarying, the same throughout, is the adjectival sense matching regular.

clue.text: Staff coat, employee's latest

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

indicators.note: latest picks the final letter of employee

explanation.surface: An office scene about a worker's newest coat and the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but here it is a ceremonial rod; 'latest' takes E from employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial staff of office, carried before an official, is this rod.

clue.text: Restaurant worker, most important — I must clear out!

indicators.note: must clear out says the I has to leave the word

parts.note: chief means principal, most important

explanation.surface: A senior figure in a restaurant declares he must leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The cook running a restaurant kitchen is one of its workers.

clue.text: Absurd behaviour of artist visiting African country ending in farce

indicators.note: visiting means calling in on, so the artist goes inside the country

parts.note: Chad is a country in north central Africa
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of farce

explanation.surface: A painter's trip to an African nation turns into a farce.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence or absurd sham, a pointless act put on for show, is this word's figurative sense.

clue.text: Tyre leading pairs in rally discuss aloud

indicators.note: leading pairs asks for the first two letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Talk about motor racing tyres at a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aloud' looks like a homophone signal, but it is simply one of the three words whose opening pair is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre with its cords running at right angles to the tread is a type in common use.

clue.text: Annual diary's back — ahead of time

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of diary is taken

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A diary returns ahead of schedule, once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening once every twelve months, annual and this word are synonyms.

clue.text: Moment for telling argument

definitions.meaning: a particular instant in time, as in 'at that stage'
a persuasive remark that makes the case, as in 'you have a good one'

explanation.surface: A time to deliver a convincing case.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an instant in time and a forceful argument in a debate.

clue.text: High quality team developed, contemporary

parts.note: class means excellence, as in a player of real class

indicators.note: developed means built up into another form, so the letters of team are rearranged

explanation.surface: A first-rate side has grown up together.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmate of the same year is a contemporary, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Bet it could be part of fence

definitions.meaning: a wager, money put on an outcome
a post driven into the ground to support a fence

explanation.surface: A wager about which bit of a fence something could be.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a gambling wager and a pointed wooden post used in fencing.

clue.text: Society pair at work, beginning in London, move up fast

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters of pair being worked into a new shape
beginning in picks the first letter of London

explanation.surface: A society couple busy at work in London see their careers rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb steeply and quickly, as prices or costs do, is to move up fast.

clue.text: Royalist, offhand

definitions.meaning: a supporter of King Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.surface: A monarchist with a casual attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the King's party in the Civil War and also means careless or dismissive.

clue.text: Democrat referring to important animal

parts.note: on means about, concerning
key means crucial, important

explanation.surface: A Democrat talks about a significant creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The donkey is the emblem of the US Democratic Party, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The domestic ass is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed with English trick? Go to new positions

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a ploy is a cunning trick

explanation.surface: A flushed Englishman tries a ruse and tells people to move.
explanation.definitionFit: To move troops or staff to fresh stations is to send them to new positions.
